documents.title: UW–Madison Guiding Principles for Generative AI in Teaching
documents.stance_why: The guidance tells instructors to set and explain their own policy ('a policy for the entire course, or ... specific instructions for individual assignments') and sets no university-wide permission or ban, so it delegates.
documents.summary: Teaching-center principles on equity, data protection, educational uses, adapting assessments, communicating with students, and handling suspected misconduct. They leave AI rules to instructors and advise against AI detectors.

units.why: The preamble says the guidance came from cross-disciplinary teams of faculty, staff, technologists and student affairs specialists, which describes how the guidance was made (P84), not a rule.
units.anchor: based on the work of cross-disciplinary teams at UW–Madison

units.why: 'Campus guidance and resources will continue to evolve' says the guidance is provisional, which is P54.
units.anchor: Campus guidance and resources will continue to evolve

units.why: The text names opportunities for multilingual students, those with writer's block or entering a new discipline, which states benefits of AI for learning (P87), not a rule.
units.anchor: opportunities for students who are multilingual, who struggle with writer’s block or writing anxiety

units.why: 'AI can generate racist, sexist, and other kinds of biased responses' names bias harms (P53), an informing statement.
units.anchor: AI can generate racist, sexist, and other kinds of biased responses

units.why: 'accessibility barriers for students with certain disabilities' raises accessibility of AI tools (P97); chosen over P53 because it concerns disability access specifically.
units.anchor: It might also present accessibility barriers for students with certain disabilities

units.why: 'some students can afford premium subscriptions while others cannot' names cost-based inequity, which is P51's equity concern.
units.anchor: some students can afford premium subscriptions while others cannot

units.why: 'provides no-cost access to several generative AI tools' is a university commitment to free access, framed 'to promote equity', so P51 (free access provided); it is also an institution-wide licensed tool offer (P92), which I did not choose because the stated point is equity.
units.anchor: To promote equity, UW–Madison provides no-cost access to several generative AI tools
units.fit_note: Also states that the university provides licensed tools institution-wide (P92).

units.why: 'Instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, as well as securing FERPA-protected data' binds instructors and admins to data protection (P50).
units.anchor: Instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, as well as
units.policy: Instructors and administrators are responsible for protecting student privacy and intellectual work, as well as securing FERPA-protected data.

units.why: 'must also follow university policies that apply to the use of generative AI' requires compliance with existing policy (P77).
units.anchor: They must also follow university policies that apply to the use of generative AI

units.why: 'Students should not be asked to submit personal information to AI tools' limits what instructors may ask of students, a data-protection rule (P50) addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: Students should not be asked to submit personal information to AI tools

units.why: 'no identifying information should be included' sets a condition on instructors using AI for feedback on student work; P50 chosen over P59 because the point is removing identifiers.
units.anchor: no identifying information should be included
units.fit_note: Specifically about instructors submitting student work for AI feedback.

units.why: 'AI should not be used as the primary source of feedback or comments to students' limits AI in feedback, a condition on AI-assisted feedback (P101).
units.anchor: AI should not be used as the primary source of feedback or comments to students

units.why: Instructors 'may communicate' that prompts and materials are protected IP and that submitting them to AI without permission might violate rights; this is a course-material upload restriction (P49), phrased for the instructor to convey.
units.anchor: submitting those materials to an AI tool without permission might be a violation of intellectual
units.policy: Instructors who are concerned about intellectual property may communicate to students that assignment prompts and other instructor-created materials are protected intellectual property, and that submitting those materials to an AI tool without permission might be a violation of intellectual property rights.
units.fit_note: Framed as something instructors may tell students, not a direct student ban.

units.why: The section 'Consider Educational Uses' says 'Generative AI can support student learning and open new opportunities for teaching', stating benefits (P87).
units.anchor: Generative AI can support student learning and open new opportunities for teaching

units.why: 'generating or testing out ideas or formulas' as a potential student use is brainstorming and exploration (P15).
units.anchor: generating or testing out ideas or formulas
units.fit_note: Same sentence also lists summarizing, genre conventions and grammar checking.

units.why: 'checking grammar' and 'learning specific genre conventions' are listed uses of AI for writing support (P91).
units.anchor: learning specific genre conventions; checking grammar

units.why: 'To clarify complex readings, issues, or points of confusion' describes using AI to understand material like a tutor (P12).
units.anchor: To clarify complex readings, issues, or points of confusion

units.why: 'finding, generating, and analyzing data quickly' is a listed student use for research and data analysis (P89).
units.anchor: finding, generating, and analyzing data quickly

units.why: 'generating websites or posters' is an AI use for multimodal communication products, closest to images and graphics (P106).
units.anchor: encouraging multimodal approaches to communication (e.g., generating websites or posters)
units.fit_note: Websites and posters, not only images and illustrations.

units.why: 'check knowledge of course content by generating practice quizzes' is a study aid use (P14).
units.anchor: To check knowledge of course content by generating practice quizzes

units.why: 'help with designing course materials, including syllabi, questions, quizzes' lists instructor uses of AI for teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: To get help with designing course materials, including syllabi, questions, quizzes, and prompts for learning
units.policy: To get help with designing course materials, including syllabi, questions, quizzes, and prompts for learning activities

units.why: 'To explain complex concepts in multiple ways for diverse learners' is a potential instructor use of AI (P59).
units.anchor: To explain complex concepts in multiple ways for diverse learners

units.why: 'generate drafts of announcements or newsletters' is a potential instructor use for course communication (P59).
units.anchor: To generate drafts of announcements or newsletters for large classes or cohorts

units.why: 'instructor feedback on an entire student work should not be automated' limits AI feedback, while AI may assist on a paragraph; this sets conditions for AI-assisted feedback (P101).
units.anchor: instructor feedback on an entire student work should not be automated

units.why: 'be prepared to share with students how you are using it' asks instructors to disclose their own AI use (P47).
units.anchor: be prepared to share with students how you are using it

units.why: 'consider how to adapt learning experiences and assessments' advises instructors to redesign assessment around AI, whether or not they use it (P35).
units.anchor: Whether or not you choose to use generative AI as the instructor, consider how to
units.policy: Whether or not you choose to use generative AI as the instructor, consider how to adapt learning experiences and assessments.

units.why: 'Think about the skills students need to develop and use independently' ties AI decisions to learning goals (P83).
units.anchor: Think about the skills students need to develop and use independently as well as the
units.policy: Think about the skills students need to develop and use independently as well as the tasks where AI is increasingly being employed as part of a discipline or profession.

units.why: 'Scaffolding learning tasks and assessments so students might feel more capable of success without relying exclusively on AI' is an assignment redesign strategy (P35).
units.anchor: Scaffolding learning tasks and assessments so students might feel more capable of success without relying
units.policy: Scaffolding learning tasks and assessments so students might feel more capable of success without relying exclusively on AI.

units.why: 'authentic assessments and activities that can be completed without AI', such as in-class discussion and peer review, is an assignment redesign recommendation (P35).
units.anchor: Developing authentic assessments and activities that can be completed without AI

units.why: 'metacognitive learning strategies, such as writers’ memos, reflections on learning' recommends reflective artifacts in assessment design (P35); P26 is for requiring students to submit reflections on AI use, which this does not say.
units.anchor: Considering metacognitive learning strategies, such as writers’ memos, reflections on learning, and sharing thinking processes

units.why: 'flipped classroom and active learning ... time in class to brainstorm or work on assignments' redesigns course structure in response to AI (P35).
units.anchor: Exploring flipped classroom and active learning opportunities using tools such as Top Hat as well
units.policy: Exploring flipped classroom and active learning opportunities using tools such as Top Hat as well as time in class to brainstorm or work on assignments.

units.why: 'holding conferences with students to gauge learning' checks understanding through meetings (P34); the same sentence also recommends version histories and check-ins.
units.anchor: holding conferences with students to gauge learning
units.fit_note: Same sentence also recommends version histories and check-ins as process-over-product design (P35).

units.why: 'sharing Google version histories ... implementing check-ins on progress' are process-over-product assessment redesigns (P35).
units.anchor: Using process-over-product approaches, such as sharing Google version histories

units.why: 'Communicate with students about generative AI ... at the start of a course ... as well as throughout the semester' tells instructors to state expectations in syllabus, Canvas and conversation (P09).
units.anchor: both at the start of a course (in course syllabi, in Canvas, and in conversation)
units.policy: Communicate with students about generative AI (including how it relates to academic integrity), both at the start of a course (in course syllabi, in Canvas, and in conversation) as well as throughout the semester.
units.fit_note: Advises communicating in syllabi, Canvas and conversation, repeatedly; not a strict syllabus requirement.

units.why: 'The proliferation of generative AI tools necessitates intentional and thoughtful discussions' advises discussing AI and integrity with students (P66).
units.anchor: necessitates intentional and thoughtful discussions about AI broadly

units.why: 'a policy for the entire course, or ... specific instructions for individual assignments' leaves the rule to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: might have a policy for the entire course, or you might have specific instructions for
units.policy: You, as the instructor, might have a policy for the entire course, or you might have specific instructions for individual assignments and assessments.

units.why: 'students might receive different guidelines from other instructors' notes rules vary by instructor, so a course's rules do not carry over (P11).
units.anchor: Recognize that students might receive different guidelines from other instructors
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to recognize variation, not a statement that rules do not transfer.

units.why: 'View sample AI Statements for Course Syllabi' points instructors to sample syllabus language (P110).
units.anchor: View sample AI Statements for Course Syllabi

units.why: 'Provide clear instructions, examples, and explanations' of the expectations is guidance to explain the rules to students (P66).
units.anchor: Provide clear instructions, examples, and explanations to help students understand the expectations

units.why: The example 'relying on AI to complete a math assignment that builds skills necessary for more advanced work' says AI can hinder skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: when AI might hinder their learning or development of essential skills and knowledge
units.fit_note: Also asks instructors to explain permitted uses (initial queries, topic development).

units.why: 'it is particularly important that you explain why to students in the context of learning outcomes' asks instructors who discourage or prohibit AI to give reasons (P66).
units.anchor: it is particularly important that you explain why to students

units.why: 'consider when/how/in what way AI-generated content should be cited' asks instructors who allow AI to set citation rules (P24).
units.anchor: consider when/how/in what way AI-generated content should be cited
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors as a design consideration, not a student requirement.

units.why: 'whether to require students to turn in, or at least retain, AI chat transcripts' is a transcript option for instructors (P26).
units.anchor: whether to require students to turn in, or at least retain, AI chat transcripts

units.why: 'Establish a clear and transparent dialogue ... to help avoid an instructor-student dynamic built on mistrust' advises tone and dialogue with students (P66).
units.anchor: Establish a clear and transparent dialogue with students early (and often)

units.why: 'Using a “misconduct” lens can create a climate of policing/suspicion' cautions against a policing posture, which is a push toward non-punitive handling (P68).
units.anchor: Using a “misconduct” lens can create a climate of policing/suspicion
units.fit_note: Cautions against a policing climate; does not itself prescribe remedial responses.

units.why: 'Incorporate the topic of generative AI into a broader discussion on academic integrity and professional ethics' asks instructors to discuss AI in class (P66).
units.anchor: Incorporate the topic of generative AI into a broader discussion on academic integrity and professional
units.policy: Incorporate the topic of generative AI into a broader discussion on academic integrity and professional ethics within the course discipline.

units.why: 'Departments are being encouraged to facilitate conversations ... to clarify shared expectations' asks for coordination of rules within a discipline (P109).
units.anchor: Departments are being encouraged to facilitate conversations within their specific discipline to clarify shared expectations

units.why: 'Academic associate deans, CTLM, and WAC are available to support these conversations' names support offered to faculty (P63).
units.anchor: Academic associate deans, CTLM, and Writing Across the Curriculum (WAC) are available to support these
units.policy: Academic associate deans, CTLM, and Writing Across the Curriculum (WAC) are available to support these conversations.

units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to take a proactive approach to prevent misconduct using the teaching and communication strategies' favors prevention through teaching (P99).
units.anchor: take a proactive approach to prevent misconduct using the teaching and communication strategies
units.fit_note: Prevention through teaching and communication rather than easing pressures like extensions.

units.why: 'Avoid generative AI detection tools; they are imperfect at best' tells instructors not to rely on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: Avoid generative AI detection tools; they are imperfect at best

units.why: 'UW–Madison has decided not to offer an enterprise tool for AI detection' states an institutional decision on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: UW–Madison has decided not to offer an enterprise tool for AI detection due to these
units.policy: UW–Madison has decided not to offer an enterprise tool for AI detection due to these issues.

units.why: 'address it as they would any case of suspected academic misconduct' places AI cases under established integrity procedures (P36).
units.anchor: they should address it as they would any case of suspected academic misconduct

units.why: 'beginning by meeting with the student to discuss concerns' tells instructors to talk with the student first (P57).
units.anchor: beginning by meeting with the student to discuss concerns

documents.unit: Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards
documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Instructors’ expectations will vary from course to course' and that students must ask if unclear; it sets no university-wide permission, so it delegates to instructors.
documents.summary: Student-conduct page stating that students must know and follow each instructor's AI expectations, ask if unsure, and that unauthorized use is raised as a possible violation of UWS 14 (unauthorized materials).

units.why: 'we expect our students to uphold the core values of academic integrity' sets honesty, trust, fairness, respect and responsibility as the grounding for AI rules (P95).
units.anchor: At UW–Madison we expect our students to uphold the core values of academic integrity which
units.policy: At UW–Madison we expect our students to uphold the core values of academic integrity which include honesty, trust, fairness, respect, and responsibility.

units.why: 'both opportunities and challenges as it relates to academic integrity' is a framing statement about AI tools and integrity (P56).
units.anchor: has afforded us both opportunities and challenges
units.fit_note: Preamble framing only; no principles are stated.

units.why: The quote from UWS Chapter 14 says students are responsible for honest completion and representation of work and appropriate citation; this is ownership of submitted work (P29).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for the honest completion and representation of their work

units.why: 'Students are responsible for knowing their instructor’s expectations when it comes to using AI tools' makes students find out each course's rules (P78).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for knowing their instructor’s expectations when it comes to using AI tools

units.why: 'it is the student’s responsibility to ask their instructor before using them' is the ask-when-unsure rule (P10).
units.anchor: it is the student’s responsibility to ask their instructor before using them

units.why: 'Instructors’ expectations will vary from course to course' says the rule is set by each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Instructors’ expectations will vary from course to course

units.why: 'If an instructor does not allow the use of AI tools and they suspect a student has used them' treats unauthorized AI use as a possible violation of UWS 14.03(1)(b) Use of Unauthorized Materials (P36).
units.anchor: possible violation of UWS 14.03(1)(b) Use of Unauthorized Materials

units.why: 'they will invite the student to meet with them' commits instructors to talking with the student about suspected misuse (P57).
units.anchor: they will invite the student to meet with them about the possible violation

units.why: 'It is your responsibility to know and follow your instructor’s expectations ... check your course syllabi, course information in Canvas' tells students to look up each course's rules (P78).
units.anchor: If unsure, check your course syllabi, course information in Canvas, or talk with your instructors
units.fit_note: Also says to ask the instructor when unsure (P10).

units.why: 'If your instructor requires you to cite AI use, Libraries provides guidance' refers students to library citation guidance (P115).
units.anchor: If your instructor requires you to cite AI use, Libraries provides guidance for how to
units.policy: If your instructor requires you to cite AI use, Libraries provides guidance for how to do this
units.fit_note: Conditional on an instructor requiring citation.

units.why: 'posting queries or text into AI tools may share that information with the broader internet community. Consider it the same as posting on a public forum' warns students about data exposure (P50).
units.anchor: Consider it the same as posting on a public forum

units.why: 'Uphold the values academic integrity' repeats the integrity grounding for AI use (P95).
units.anchor: Uphold the values academic integrity

units.why: 'they should contact you directly to have a meeting about their concerns' tells students instructors will meet with them first (P57).
units.anchor: contact you directly to have a meeting about their concerns

units.why: 'Connect with staff within the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards to help you navigate the process' directs students to a human office for help (P72).
units.anchor: Connect with staff within the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards to help you
units.policy: Connect with staff within the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards to help you navigate the process.

documents.title: Generative AI at UW–Madison: Use Policies
documents.stance_why: The page sets data and security limits on all users (e.g. 'You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data') but says nothing on whether AI is allowed for coursework, so it sets no course-level stance and delegates.
documents.summary: IT policy page listing prohibited generative AI uses tied to existing data, security, harassment and copyright policies, plus incident reporting and a pointer to trustworthy-AI criteria.

units.why: 'This page outlines existing policies governing what you may and may not do' and 'These policies safeguard institutional data' states the purpose and scope of the page (P56).
units.anchor: These policies safeguard institutional data, which everyone in the university is legally and ethically obligated
units.policy: These policies safeguard institutional data, which everyone in the university is legally and ethically obligated to protect.

units.why: 'All university faculty, staff, students and affiliates must follow these policies' sets who is bound, a scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: All university faculty, staff, students and affiliates must follow these policies
units.fit_note: Scope statement; no principle content.

units.why: 'you must follow UW–Madison, UWSA and UW System Board of Regents policies when using generative AI tools' requires compliance with existing policy (P77).
units.anchor: you must follow UW–‍Madison, UW System Administration (UWSA) and UW System Board of Regents policies

units.why: 'You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review' bans entering protected data and ties use to review (P50).
units.anchor: You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI
units.policy: You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review

units.why: 'Work produced by students to satisfy course requirements' is on the list of FERPA data that may not be entered into AI tools, closest to a ban on uploading student work and course material (P49).
units.anchor: Work produced by students to satisfy course requirements
units.policy: Work produced by students to satisfy course requirements is protected data that may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.
units.fit_note: Concerns student work as protected data rather than students uploading course materials.

units.why: 'Student names and grades' are listed protected data that may not be entered into AI tools (P50).
units.anchor: Student names and grades
units.policy: Student names and grades are protected data that may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.

units.why: 'Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals' may not be entered into AI tools, a research-confidentiality rule (P62).
units.anchor: Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals
units.policy: Material under confidential review, including research papers and funding proposals, may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.

units.why: 'Intellectual property not publicly available' is listed data that may not be entered into AI tools; P50 chosen as the core is data protection, though P52 also touches IP.
units.anchor: Intellectual property not publicly available
units.policy: Intellectual property that is not publicly available may not be entered into a generative AI tool or service unless it has undergone appropriate internal review.

units.why: 'You may not upload any information from electronic files you are not authorized to access and use' bans unauthorized uploads, grounded in UW-870 (P77).
units.anchor: You may not upload any information from electronic files you are not authorized to access
units.policy: You may not upload any information from electronic files you are not authorized to access and use.
units.fit_note: A data-access rule tied to an existing policy.

units.why: 'You may not upload any data that could be used to help create or carry out malware, spam and phishing campaigns' bans malicious use of AI (P74).
units.anchor: You may not upload any data that could be used to help create or carry
units.policy: You may not upload any data that could be used to help create or carry out malware, spam and phishing campaigns or other cyber scams.

units.why: 'You may not upload aerial photographs or scaled drawings of UW–Madison areas or utilities-related data' bans uploading security-sensitive facility data (P50).
units.anchor: You may not upload aerial photographs or scaled drawings of UW–‍Madison areas or utilities-related data
units.fit_note: Facility security data rather than personal data.

units.why: 'without having it reviewed by a human to verify it doesn’t have malicious elements' requires human review of AI-generated code in IT systems (P31, verify AI output).
units.anchor: You may not use AI-generated code within institutional IT systems or services without having it
units.policy: You may not use AI-generated code within institutional IT systems or services without having it reviewed by a human to verify it doesn’t have malicious elements.
units.fit_note: Applies to code in institutional IT systems, with a security reason.

units.why: 'You may not direct AI tools or services to generate content that facilitates sexual harassment, stalking or sexual exploitation' bans harmful generation (P74).
units.anchor: You may not direct AI tools or services to generate content that facilitates sexual harassment,
units.policy: You may not direct AI tools or services to generate content that facilitates sexual harassment, stalking or sexual exploitation.

units.why: 'generate content that helps others break federal, state or local laws; institutional policies ... or licensing agreements' bans using AI to help break laws or rules (P74).
units.anchor: You may not use AI tools or services to generate content that helps others break
units.policy: You may not use AI tools or services to generate content that helps others break federal, state or local laws; institutional policies, rules or guidelines; or licensing agreements or contracts.

units.why: 'generate content that enables harassment, threats, defamation, hostile environments, stalking or illegal discrimination' bans harmful generation (P74).
units.anchor: You may not use AI tools or services to generate content that enables harassment, threats,
units.policy: You may not use AI tools or services to generate content that enables harassment, threats, defamation, hostile environments, stalking or illegal discrimination.

units.why: 'You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property rights' is a copyright rule (P52).
units.anchor: You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property
units.policy: You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property rights.

units.why: 'Entering copyrighted material ... may effectively result in the creation of a digital copy' explains the copyright risk (P52).
units.anchor: may effectively result in the creation of a digital copy, which is a copyright violation

units.why: 'entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature disclosure, compromising invention patentability' is a research IP risk (P52).
units.anchor: In addition, entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature
units.policy: In addition, entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature disclosure, compromising invention patentability.

units.why: 'many of the above uses also violate generative AI providers’ policies and terms' notes provider terms of use (P52).
units.anchor: In addition to violating UW policies, many of the above uses also violate generative AI
units.policy: In addition to violating UW policies, many of the above uses also violate generative AI providers’ policies and terms.
units.fit_note: Provider terms, not copyright or ownership as such.

units.why: 'must report the incident' creates a duty for anyone who learns of a data breach, including through generative AI, to report it (P71).
units.anchor: must report the incident

units.why: 'choosing tools and services that exhibit ... characteristics of trustworthy AI' encourages users to evaluate and select tools by trustworthiness criteria (P117).
units.anchor: choosing tools and services that exhibit

units.why: 'Contact Heather Johnston, IT policy writer & analyst, Office of Cybersecurity' names who answers questions on AI use and policies (P80).
units.anchor: Contact Heather Johnston, IT policy writer & analyst, Office of Cybersecurity
units.fit_note: Names a contact for questions, not an enforcement owner.

units.why: The 'Additional AI resources' list links to teaching, student conduct, copyright and CISO guidance (P115).
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (UW–‍Madison Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards)

units.why: 'Version 3, published August 23, 2024' records the version and date of this policy page (P84).
units.anchor: Version 3, published August 23, 2024
units.fit_note: Only a version and date; no description of the process.

notes: Coder A. Three university-layer documents; no school, computing or course documents were included in the collect file.
